ai.description: *Indirana longicrus* is a slender frog reaching 30–40 mm. It is brown with a dark lateral stripe and possesses exceptionally long, thin hind limbs. It lacks vocal sacs and exhibits a pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana longicrus* is best distinguished by its exceptionally long, slender hind limbs, which extend well beyond the snout when pressed along the body.
ai.habitat: *Indirana longicrus* inhabits the leaf litter and rocky stream banks of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kempholey bubble-nest frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the damp, rocky stream banks of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana longicrus* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying clutches of 100–200 eggs in mossy, semi-aquatic habitats where larvae develop in thin films of water.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana longicrus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kempholey Bubble-nest Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "tink" notes, typically heard near rocky streams within its humid forest habitat.
